1. General summary Using adapted Oil&Gas (O&G) platform designs for floating wind is a reliable solution
but too expensive for the wind sector. There is a need to redesign floating solutions to
reduce the LCOE to competitive levels compared to fixed solutions. X1Wind is
developing an innovative weathervaning system to reduce drastically the weight and
costs of current solutions: the PivotBuoy. The PivotBuoy is a novel system integrating
the mooring, the anchoring and the electrical cable in a single point (single point
mooring – SPM) allowing a faster connection of floating platforms.
The PivotBuoy brings the stability and light weight of tension-leg systems (TLPs) but
can be combined with the simpler installation strategy of ‘onshore assembly and tug to
site’ of semi-submersibles. As a result, the PivotBuoy can be easily pre-installed, while
the floating platform is towed to site with local vessels (avoiding the need for large
expensive vessels) and easily connected to the mini-TLP. By using a downwind
configuration, a more efficient structure can be designed, which enables to eliminate
the tower and drastically reduce the platform weight, achieving around 260 tons/MW
(similar to fixed offshore) while spar and semi-submersibles require between 1.000 and
2.000 tons/MW. Using a truss structure not only allows to reduce platform weight, but
also to minimize wave slamming and wind turbulence that traditional tubular towers
induce in a downwind rotor.
The weight reduction and the installation strategy reduce the capital expenditures
(CAPEX) by around 50% compared to the state-of-the-art floating wind.
2. Method
After completing the conceptual design phase and simulations with the Orcaflex model,
a successful proof of concept was conducted with a 1:64 scale prototype of the X1Wind
downwind platform and the PivotBuoy at CIEMLAB wave flume (UPC, Barcelona) to
validate the model. Regular wave periods were tested as well as extreme conditions,
and up to 90º of wind/waves misalignment, and they confirmed that the stability given
by the PivotBuoy is comparable with only a fraction of the weight of semi-submersibles
or spar platforms using catenary moorings (much heavier).
The next tank tests will be conducted in February through de MariNET2 Programme in
the Hydrodynamic and Ocean Engineering tank of ECN (Ecole Centrale Nantes), the
results of which will also be presented at the conference. 3. Results
Tests showed that the dynamic behaviour of the system matched well the Orcaflex
simulation model. Results also showed that while other floating platforms with different
mooring systems are 3 to 6 times heavier, PivotBuoy has similar or improved stability
performance. While spar and semi-submersibles have a slight improvement in heave
and pitch motion (with large weight increase), they have a much larger wave-induced
surge motion, that will affect negatively on thrust variation and turbine torque stability.
Additionally, results from ongoing projects (e.g. IEA WIND Task 40) show that
downwind rotors can bring additional 5-8% reduction of LCOE for large-scale turbines,
as they don’t require pre-coning and blade pre-bending (unlike upwind rotors to avoid
tower strike), allowing lighter and larger blades, increasing the energy production.
4. Conclusions
The PivotBuoy is a new SPM system that can be implemented in deep waters with a
cost similar to fixed offshore, making floating wind cost-effective. It has the potential to
lower the CAPEX of a downwind floating platform by more than 50%, and the OPEX up
to 20%. These significant cost reductions are achieved through mooring and anchoring
cost reduction (instead of long and heavy catenary chains), a low-cost and efficient
novel connection (avoiding traditional complex turrets), enabling platform weight
reduction, and allowing assembly and installation using local infrastructure.
5. Learning Objectives
The SPM technology has been widely used in O&G for decades, specifically for the
connection of FPSOs (Floating Production, Storage and Offloading), but remains
unknown to the majority of the wind industry. A few new entrants in the floating wind
sector are proposing to use SPM technology to connect their floating platforms (Eolink,
Saitec, X1Wind, Hexicon, and Tetrafloat). Delegates will learn what are the advantages
of implementing this technology with floating offshore wind platforms, like the drastic
weight and LCOE reduction or the elimination of active systems, as well as the
challenges (such as the possible misalignment of wind and waves) in comparison to
current mooring solutions.
source.title: PivotBuoy: An Advanced System for Cost-effective and Reliable Mooring, Connection, Installation and Operation of Floating Wind
